text:
Lina: Hey team, just got a P1 from AcmeCorp — embeddings requests from their EU app are showing very high 95p latency and some responses routed to us-west. They say throughput drops during peaks and some vectors look wrong (dims changed). Can we triage?

Maya: Acked — ticket #INC-8721. Customer says calls include region=eu-west-1 in the payload but response header shows X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2. Latency spikes align with their peak at ~08:30 UTC.

Jamal: @Maya can you paste a sample request/response? I want to check routing decision logs.

Maya: Pasting sanitized curl from customer:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-1536","region":"eu-west-1","input":["text A","text B"]}'
```
Response headers: `X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2`, `x-request-id: r-0a1b2c`. Body is fine but tokenization seems delayed. Customer also saw an occasional dimension mismatch error: `expected 1536 got 1280` on retry.

Jamal: Thanks. Looking at router logs for `r-0a1b2c`: routing decision: region=eu-west-1 -> candidate pool eu-1 (capacity exhausted) -> fallback policy: cross-region-route -> assigned us-west-2-pool-7. Spillover_count++ -> cold start triggered on us-west-2 instance. Cold start + VM spin-up explains 2s+ latency.

OpsBot: [auto] scaling event: eu-1 pool at 100% utilization, queued requests: 54, spillover triggered at 1943210123.

Raj: That matches. We had a scheduled maintenance window earlier this morning that reduced eu-1 spare capacity by the autoscaler threshold. Shouldn't have impacted dedicated customers but looks like routing policy allowed cross-region fallback for this customer (they're on tier 'standard').

Lina: Customer says they explicitly set `region` and expected hard route. Can we confirm whether user-specified region is a strict hint or just preferred?

Jamal: Current behavior: `region` is a preferred region by default. For dedicated/reserved capacity accounts there's a `pin_region=true` option but customer didn't set it. We probably need to make this clearer in API and default stricter for high-commit accounts.

Maya: Repro steps I ran from EU proxy:
1) Send 100 concurrent embed requests with `region=eu-west-1` and model `embed-lite-1536`
2) Observe router decisions and target pool metrics
3) I saw ~12% of requests routed to us-west-2 when eu pool saturated, and those had cold-start latency 1500-2500ms.

Jamal: Also noticed batching behavior: some cross-region fallbacks cause heterogeneous batch composition which can trigger quantization/dimension errors on the runtime if model variant mismatches. That explains the `expected 1536 got 1280` error on retries. The pipeline attempts a compatible variant in fallback region but model flavor differs (embed-lite-1536 vs embed-legacy-1280).

Raj: That's a bug — router should only pick a fallback that matches model family/dimension. Otherwise we must reject and return 409 or explicit error, not attempt a cross-model call.

Lina: Customer is upset about both latency and inconsistent vectors. They flagged potential billing impact due to cross-region egress. They want a timeline.

Maya: Short-term mitigation I proposed to them: add `pin_region=true` to requests or set account-level region pin in Console under "Routing" which forces hard route (no cross-region fallback). Also temporarily increase eu reserved capacity from dashboard to avoid spillover.

Jamal: Concretely for infra:
- Patch router to include model-dimension check in fallback decision (if dims mismatch, skip pool).
- Add metric `routing.fallback.model_mismatch` to alert.
- Make `region` option semantics more explicit in docs and SDK (hint vs pin).

Raj: I'll open a deployment PR to change fallback policy for `standard` tier to prefer a reject-over-fallback for embeddings models that are dimension-sensitive. Will also add a rate-limiter to prevent sudden queue spikes causing multi-pool spillover.

deploy-bot: [auto] Created PR #3214 by Raj: "router: avoid cross-model fallback for embeddings; add model dimension guard". CI queued.

Jamal: For the dimension mismatch errors, we should also add a defensive runtime check that returns a clear error (400/409) with `expected_dim` and `actual_dim` fields, instead of sometimes returning truncated vectors.

Maya: Customer accepted temporary pin_region and increased reserved capacity; will monitor. They asked for ETA on fix.

Raj: ETA: patch to router + metric + docs — target hotfix in 48 hours if CI/QA passes. Longer-term: account-level policy controls and proactive autoscaler tweaks (1-2 weeks).

Lina: I've updated ticket with mitigations and gave customer 48h ETA. Also added repro logs and sample curl.

Maya: Follow-up items for postmortem:
- Why maintenance reduced eu spare capacity unexpectedly
- Router fallback policy test coverage for model family matching
- Billing/egress visibility when cross-region fallback occurs

Jamal: I'll attach routing decision trace for r-0a1b2c to the incident. Trace excerpt:
```
{"ts":1943210123, "req":"r-0a1b2c", "pref_region":"eu-west-1", "pools_tried":["eu-1:100%","us-west-2:spinup"], "decision":"fallback", "reason":"eu-full", "selected_pool":"us-west-2-pool-7", "model_check":"mismatch:1536!=1280"}
```
OpsBot: [auto] incident severity bumped to Sev-2 at 1943210300 (customer-impacting), assigned to oncall @Jamal.

Lina: Great work. I'll run the customer call summary in 30m and confirm they set pin_region. Keep me posted on PR progress.

Raj: I'll jump on CI fixes now. If anyone sees more customers affected, drop their request ids here.

Maya: Thanks all. Closing loop with Acme in 45m after we confirm metrics. :thumbsup:
